scope.summary: The LeaseRegistry is already wired into the widget-mutation RPC path, but its exclusive guard ends after dispatch while ActionChannel keeps the same target busy until post-render acknowledgement. A later agent can therefore acquire the registry lease and immediately receive ActionError::TargetBusy from the still-busy channel. Align the two serialization windows by retaining the per-target registry guard while boundedly retrying only the channel's typed TargetBusy response above the ActionChannel borrow; release the channel mutex before every await and preserve ActionChannel as the terminal-lifetime authority.

evidence.registry_call_sites: mcp/session.rs routes click_widget and set_value through DispatchPlan::ExclusiveWrite and calls LeaseRegistry::try_acquire on the synchronous path and LeaseRegistry::acquire_async on the shared async server path.
evidence.window_mismatch: The registry guard is released when dispatch returns, while ActionChannel::enqueue scans queue plus in_flight and returns ActionError::TargetBusy until post-render acknowledgement. The second serialization window outlives the first.
evidence.the_failing_proof: test_swarm_concurrency::test_swarm_concurrency_n5. Its own comment states the contract: "Under a generous timeout the lease only WAITS; every mutation must enqueue." All five agents target shell.chrome.theme-toggle / the rail input concurrently, and agents 0, 1 and 2 each got {"code":-32004,"message":"widget 'shell.chrome.theme-toggle' already has an unacknowledged mutation"} on action 0. The test asserts queued == true.
evidence.the_registry_already_does_the_right_thin: leases.rs provides waiting acquisition and a timeout backstop. The missing behavior is a bounded wait for the longer-lived ActionChannel transaction after the registry lease has been acquired.

the_constraint_that_makes_this_architect.why_a_retry_loop_inside_dispatch_request: dispatch_request (tools.rs:344-350) is SYNCHRONOUS and holds `channel: &mut ActionChannel` for its whole body. Waiting there would block while holding the exclusive borrow the frame loop needs in order to drain the queue and RELEASE the very lease being waited on. It would not merely be slow - it would deadlock.
the_constraint_that_makes_this_architect.where_the_wait_must_live: In McpSession::dispatch_shared_async, above each short ActionChannel mutex borrow. Each retry attempt may resolve and enqueue while holding the mutex, but the mutex must be dropped before the async delay so the frame loop can acknowledge the prior action.
the_constraint_that_makes_this_architect.guard_lifetime_decision: Keep ActionChannel queue plus in_flight state as the authority from successful enqueue through terminal acknowledgement. Hold the registry guard across bounded TargetBusy retries only until the new action enqueues or the single request deadline expires. This forms a gap-free handoff: while retrying the registry guard excludes another session; enqueue records the new channel transaction while the channel mutex is held; after enqueue the channel transaction already excludes the target before the registry guard drops. Carrying a registry guard inside pending/in_flight records would duplicate ActionChannel's established terminal-lifetime authority and couple the async lease registry to render acknowledgement without adding exclusion.

acceptance_criteria.AC-134-1: After winning the per-widget registry lease, a mutating RPC that encounters ActionChannel::TargetBusy waits and retries instead of returning -32004 immediately. Registry acquisition plus channel-busy retries share one documented request deadline, and no ActionChannel mutex guard or borrow is held across an await.
acceptance_criteria.AC-134-2: test_swarm_concurrency::test_swarm_concurrency_n5 passes: five concurrent agents, every mutation enqueued, no torn state, each response carrying its own agent_id.
acceptance_criteria.AC-134-3: The single request deadline still fires for both registry contention and a channel transaction that remains busy. Prove both paths return typed -32004 within the configured bound; a wait that can never time out is a hang, not a fix.
acceptance_criteria.AC-134-4: No ActionChannel mutex guard or borrow is held across an await. The change remains per-resource: two agents targeting different widgets do not wait on each other's registry lease, and no new multi-key ordering is introduced.
acceptance_criteria.AC-134-5: The guard lifetime decision is recorded in scope.the_constraint_that_makes_this_architectural.guard_lifetime_decision and the implementation preserves that gap-free registry-to-channel handoff.
acceptance_criteria.AC-134-6: The in-product UserManual states that same-widget mutations wait until the current post-render acknowledgement completes, may return typed -32004 at the bounded deadline, and different-widget mutations remain independently leased.

proof_targets.PT-134-2: Focused RED-path tests show both a held registry lease and a persistently busy ActionChannel return typed -32004 within the configured single request deadline.
proof_targets.PT-134-3: A concurrency proof that two agents targeting DIFFERENT widgets never block each other - otherwise the fix has serialized the whole surface instead of per-resource leasing.

scope.risk_if_missed: HBR-SWARM parallel steering does not work under contention. Same-widget agents lose actions during the registry-to-channel lifetime gap even though both serialization mechanisms individually work.

CORRECTION_2026_08_13.what_was_wrong: This MT was filed claiming the MT-028 LeaseRegistry has ZERO call sites and was "built and never connected". That is FALSE. The registry IS wired, through mcp/session.rs: try_acquire at :199 (SharedRead on the snapshot resource) and :216 (ExclusiveWrite on the per-widget target key), driven by SwarmSession::decide (:147-166) which routes click_widget / set_value with a non-empty target to DispatchPlan::ExclusiveWrite.
CORRECTION_2026_08_13.how_the_error_was_made: The originating investigation grepped for acquire_all and .acquire( and found nothing outside leases.rs. The real API in use is try_acquire, which the grep never matched. A negative result from one spelling was treated as proof of absence. Recorded because the same mistake is cheap to repeat.

what_is_actually_true.the_lease_does_wait: LeaseRegistry::try_acquire (leases.rs:162-176) loops until a deadline, so the "generous timeout only WAITS" contract the test states IS implemented for the lease.
what_is_actually_true.the_second_mechanism_does_not: There are TWO serialization mechanisms with DIFFERENT lifetimes. The lease guard is released at the END of SwarmSession::dispatch (session.rs documents this: "The registry lease guard drops at the end of this call"). The ActionChannel then keeps its own per-target in-flight transaction until POST-RENDER acknowledgement, and that second mechanism fails FAST: ActionChannel::enqueue scans queue + in_flight and returns ActionError::TargetBusy immediately (action.rs:1077-1093), which tools.rs:314 maps to the same -32004.
what_is_actually_true.consequence: A second agent can win the lease - because the first agent already released it at dispatch end - and then still be rejected by the channel because the first action has not been acknowledged yet. The wait protects the wrong window. That is why test_swarm_concurrency sees -32004 on action 0 for agents 0, 1 and 2 despite a generous lease timeout.

CORRECTION_2026_08_13.what_this_MT_should_actually_decide: Whether the exclusive lease should be HELD until the action terminalizes (aligning the two windows, so the wait covers the period that actually blocks), or whether the channel TargetBusy should itself become a bounded wait. The first is a lifetime change to the guard; the second changes fail-fast semantics inside the channel. Either way the earlier framing - "wire up an unwired registry" - is not the work.
CORRECTION_2026_08_13.what_survives_from_the_original_filing: The deadlock CONSTRAINT still holds and is still the trap: dispatch_request (tools.rs:344-350) is synchronous and holds &mut ActionChannel for its whole body, so a wait placed there blocks the frame loop that would release what is being waited on. Any fix that lengthens a hold must not lengthen it across that borrow.
CORRECTION_2026_08_13.status_note: SUPERSEDED by RESCOPE_2026_08_13 after operator granted scope expansion; the canonical scope summary, evidence, design decision, acceptance criteria, proof targets, and allowed paths above are now re-authored against the verified two-window mechanism.

RESCOPE_2026_08_13.operator_authority: Scope expansion explicitly granted in the live 2026-08-14 objective for all rescope MTs.
RESCOPE_2026_08_13.selected_approach: Bounded TargetBusy retry in McpSession::dispatch_shared_async while retaining the per-target registry guard and dropping the ActionChannel mutex before every await.
RESCOPE_2026_08_13.rejected_approach: Attaching LeaseGuard to ActionChannel pending/in_flight records was rejected because ActionChannel already owns terminal-lifetime exclusion; duplicating that ownership would couple rendering acknowledgement to the registry without closing an additional race.
RESCOPE_2026_08_13.deadline_contract: Registry acquisition and channel-busy retry consume one request deadline derived from McpSession::lease_timeout.
RESCOPE_2026_08_13.proof_contract: n5 same-widget success, registry-timeout -32004, channel-busy-timeout -32004, different-widget independence, and UserManual self-consistency.

publication_handoff_scope_expansion.reason: Gap-free snapshot-to-channel serialization requires the production post-render publisher to hold the snapshot lock while acknowledging ActionChannel transactions and publishing that same tree. Without this path, a waiter can observe target-free channel state against the pre-render snapshot.

lifecycle.creation_reason: Isolated while clearing MT-108 AC-108-3. test_swarm_concurrency was UNROUTED in the MT-127 table; root-caused to the MT-028 lease registry having zero call sites. Not fixed inline because the wait cannot live where the failure surfaces - dispatch_request holds &mut ActionChannel, so waiting there deadlocks against the frame loop that would release the lease. That is a design decision, not a patch. CORRECTED 2026-08-13: the premise was wrong. The registry IS wired via try_acquire in session.rs; the original investigation grepped only for acquire_all / .acquire( and treated that negative as proof of absence. See scope.CORRECTION_2026_08_13 for what is actually true.

implementation_result.result: The async mutation path retains the per-target registry guard while retrying only provenance-tagged ActionChannel TargetBusy responses. Snapshot and channel acquisition are nonblocking, ordered snapshot-to-channel, and share one absolute deadline. The post-render publisher acknowledges and publishes under the same ordered critical section, closing stale-tree enqueue.
implementation_result.runtime_proof: test_swarm_concurrency: 11 passed / 0 failed. n5 completed all 100 mutations with five distinct attributed agents and zero lease leaks; three additional isolated repetitions completed in 7.07s, 6.68s, and 6.48s, followed by a full-suite n5 at 6.89s. Held registry, held snapshot, held channel, persistent TargetBusy, combined registry-to-channel deadline, fresh disabled target, and different-widget paths all passed.
